## Why

`Task.task_id: int` (`domain/model.py:197`) is a plain int at every layer, and
the pre-persistence shape is a fiction: `application/submit_task.py:81`
constructs `Task(task_id=0, label=..., context=..., status=TaskStatus.TO_DO)`
and hands it to `TaskRepository.insert`, whose contract explicitly says
*"task_id is ignored, generated by DB"* (`infra/persistence/postgres.py:159`).
So the same `Task` class represents two states — pre-persistence (`task_id=0`
sentinel) and post-persistence (real SERIAL id) — and the type system cannot
tell them apart. The `task_id=0` sentinel is a load-bearing magic value that
must be remembered at every construction site (~30+ in integration tests alone).

This is the **exact Task-side analog of the `add-node-id-identity` change**
(frozen proposal), which introduced `NodeId` + `NewNode`/`Node` for
`yascheduler_nodes`. That proposal even cites `TaskRepository.insert(task) ->
Task` as the consistency anchor its own `NodeRepository.insert` mirrors — yet
`Task` itself still carries the `task_id=0` fiction. This change closes that
gap and makes `Task` consistent with the `Node`/`NewNode`/`NodeId` pattern.

The decision is **Scope B**: the domain is type-safe end-to-end (`TaskId` on
`Task`, events, exceptions, and all repository methods), and the public
`Yascheduler` facade is the **sole** `int`/`TaskId` boundary (both directions).
This keeps the `int`/`TaskId` conversion in exactly one layer rather than
scattering `.value` extractions across `Task.with_event` and every lifecycle
method (which Scope A would require).

Unlike the Node change, **no DB migration is needed**: `yascheduler_tasks.task_id
SERIAL PRIMARY KEY` already exists, and `task/insert.sql` already ends with
`RETURNING task_id, label, ip, status, metadata`. This is a pure
domain/application-layer change.

## What Changes

- **Domain split — `NewTask` / `Task` / `TaskId`** (in `yascheduler/domain/model.py`,
  exported from `yascheduler.domain`):
  - `TaskId` — `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with `value: int`; `__post_init__`
    asserts `value > 0` (SERIAL starts at 1), raising `ValueError` otherwise;
    `__str__` returns `str(self.value)` so CLI and logging render cleanly. Frozen
    → hashable → usable as a dict key. NOT equal to bare `int` (the type-safety
    point). Direct copy of `NodeId`.
  - `NewTask` — frozen dataclass: `label: str`, `context: TaskContext`,
    `status: TaskStatus = TaskStatus.TO_DO`, `allocated_ip: str | None = None` —
    the pre-persistence shape (NO `task_id`, NO `_events`). A pure data carrier:
    it has **no lifecycle methods** (those are nonsensical on an unpersisted
    task and stay on `Task`).
  - `Task` — frozen dataclass: `task_id: TaskId` (first field, identity first),
    then `label`, `context`, `status=TaskStatus.TO_DO`, `allocated_ip=None`,
    `_events: tuple[DomainEvent, ...] = field(default=(), repr=False)` — the
    post-persistence shape. A `Task` always carries its identity. Lifecycle
    methods (`allocate_to`, `mark_running`, `complete`, `fail`, `reject`,
    `with_context`, `with_event`, `pull_events`, `record_event`) are unchanged in
    behavior; `with_event` now passes `self.task_id` (a `TaskId`) to the event
    constructor with no `.value` extraction.
  - Conversion from `NewTask` to `Task` happens in **exactly one place**:
    `TaskRepository.insert` (the method that persists and receives the generated
    id).

- **Domain events** (`yascheduler/domain/events.py`): `DomainEvent.task_id:
  int -> task_id: TaskId`; all 5 subclasses (`TaskCreated`, `TaskAllocated`,
  `TaskCompleted`, `TaskFailed`, `TaskAbandoned`) inherit the new type.
  `Task.with_event` constructs events with `task_id=self.task_id` (already
  `TaskId` — no `.value` needed). `event.task_id` IS serialized into the webhook
  body — see the webhook-handler bullet below.

- **Webhook handler** (`yascheduler/infra/notifier/webhook.py`):
  `webhook_handler` (`webhook.py:74`) builds `WebhookPayload(task_id=
  event.task_id, status=status.value, custom_params=event.webhook_custom_params)`
  (`webhook.py:85-89`) and `_send_webhook` serializes it via
  `dataclasses.asdict(payload)` into the HTTP POST body (`webhook.py:112`). Since
  `event.task_id` is now a `TaskId`, line 86 MUST extract `.value`:
  `task_id=event.task_id.value` — otherwise `asdict` recurses into the `TaskId`
  dataclass and the body becomes `{"task_id": {"value": 42}, ...}` instead of
  `{"task_id": 42, ...}` (a runtime wire-shape break). `WebhookPayload.task_id:
  int` (`webhook.py:48`) stays `int` (the correct target type). The wire payload
  shape is thus preserved; this is a one-line `.value` extraction, not a behavior
  change. The handler is wired for all 5 event types at `entrypoints/di.py:120`.

- **Domain exceptions** (`yascheduler/domain/exceptions.py`): the 6 task-keyed
  exceptions — `TaskAlreadyAllocatedError`, `TaskNotAllocatedError`,
  `TaskNotTodoError`, `TaskNotRunningError`, `NoCompatibleNodeError`,
  `CloudCapacityExhaustedError` — take `task_id: TaskId` (was `int`). Their
  `f"task {task_id} ..."` messages render cleanly via `TaskId.__str__`.

- **Infra exception** (`yascheduler/infra/persistence/exceptions.py`):
  `TaskRowNotFoundError(task_id: TaskId)` (was `int`); message renders via
  `__str__`.

- **`TaskRepository` Protocol** (`yascheduler/domain/ports.py`):
  - `insert(task: Task) -> Task` → `insert(new_task: NewTask) -> Task`.
  - `get(task_id: int) -> Task | None` → `get(task_id: TaskId) -> Task | None`.
  - `update_status(task_id: int, status: TaskStatus) -> None` →
    `update_status(task_id: TaskId, status: TaskStatus) -> None`.
  - `list_ids_by_ip_and_status(...) -> list[int]` →
    `list_ids_by_ip_and_status(...) -> list[TaskId]`.
  - `list_by_jobs(job_ids: list[int]) -> list[Task]` →
    `list_by_jobs(job_ids: list[TaskId]) -> list[Task]`.
  - `save(task: Task) -> None` and `list_by_status`/`count_by_status` are
    unchanged in signature (they take/return `Task`, which now carries `TaskId`
    internally).

- **`PostgresTaskRepository`** (`yascheduler/infra/persistence/postgres.py`):
  - `insert(new_task: NewTask) -> Task` — runs `task/insert.sql ... RETURNING
    task_id` (already present), builds `Task(task_id=TaskId(int(rows[0]
    ["task_id"])), ...)` via `_row_to_task`.
  - `get(task_id: TaskId)`, `update_status(task_id: TaskId, ...)` — pass
    `task_id.value` as the SQL param (pg8000 cannot adapt a dataclass; same
    approach as `add-node-id-identity`'s `get_by_id(node_id)`).
  - `save(task)` — passes `task.task_id.value` to `update_by_id.sql`.
  - `list_ids_by_ip_and_status` — returns `[TaskId(int(row["task_id"])) for
    row in rows]`.
  - `list_by_jobs(job_ids: list[TaskId])` — passes
    `[tid.value for tid in job_ids]` as the SQL param; returns `[Task]` via
    `_row_to_task`.
  - `_row_to_task` — wraps `TaskId(int(row["task_id"]))`.

- **Use cases** (`yascheduler/application/`):
  - `submit_task` return type `int -> TaskId`. Body builds
    `NewTask(label=label, context=context)` (status/allocated_ip default) →
    `insert` → `Task` → `with_context(remote_folder based on task.task_id)` →
    `with_event(TaskCreated, ...)` → `save` → return `task.task_id` (`TaskId`).
  - `allocate_task(task_id: TaskId, ...)` and `consume_task(task_id: TaskId,
    ...)` — entry param `int -> TaskId`. They call `uow.tasks.get(task_id)`
    (now `TaskId`); logging `task_id=%s` renders via `__str__`; the orchestrator
    tracker keys become `TaskId` (internal, no boundary crossing).
  - `query_tasks(jobs: Sequence[int] | None, ...) -> list[Task]` →
    `query_tasks(jobs: Sequence[TaskId] | None, ...) -> list[Task]`. It forwards
    `list(jobs)` to `uow.tasks.list_by_jobs(list[TaskId])`. The facade
    `queue_get_tasks_async(jobs: list[int])` wraps `[TaskId(i) for i in jobs]`
    before calling `query_tasks` (this is the facade's int→TaskId marshalling,
    see below). The `statuses` branch is unaffected.

- **Public `Yascheduler` facade** (`yascheduler/entrypoints/client.py`) —
  UNCHANGED public signatures:
  - `queue_submit_task(...) -> int` (stays `int`); wraps `submit_task` and
    returns `(await submit_task(...)).value`.
  - `queue_get_task(task_id: int)` / `queue_get_tasks(jobs: list[int])` /
    `queue_get_task_async(task_id: int)` — wrap input as `TaskId(task_id)` /
    `[TaskId(i) for i in jobs]`; build the returned dict with
    `"task_id": task.task_id.value` (so the public dict keeps `int`).
  The facade is the **sole** int/TaskId marshalling layer. Concretely, the
  private `_task_to_dict(t: Task) -> Mapping` helper (`client.py:89`) — which
  builds the public `{"task_id": t.task_id, "label": ..., "ip": ...,
  "status": ..., "metadata": ...}` dict — extracts `.value`:
  `"task_id": t.task_id.value` (so the public dict stays `int`-typed).

- **CLIs**:
  - `yasubmit` (`entrypoints/cli/submit.py`): `print(str(task_id))` — `TaskId.
    __str__` renders the bare integer; no change to the print line (the value
    is now `TaskId` but renders identically).
  - `yastatus` (`entrypoints/cli/check_status.py`): three renderers and one
    query helper. `_render_default` (`f"{task.task_id}   {task.status.name}"`,
    line 145) and `_render_info` (`"task_id={}\t...".format(task.task_id, ...)`,
    line 159) render via `__str__`/`str.format` — **unchanged**. The JSON
    renderer `_render_json` (`"task_id": task.task_id` at line 181, then
    `json.dumps(objects)`) does NOT call `__str__` — `json.dumps` on a frozen
    dataclass raises `TypeError: Object of type TaskId is not JSON serializable`.
    So line 181 MUST extract `.value`: `"task_id": task.task_id.value`. The
    query helper `_query_tasks` (line 127) passes `args.jobs` (a `list[int]`
    from argparse) directly to `uow.tasks.list_by_jobs(job_ids=...)`; now that
    `list_by_jobs` takes `list[TaskId]`, line 127 becomes
    `[TaskId(j) for j in args.jobs]` (CLI-internal int→TaskId wrapping, same
    pattern as the facade's `queue_get_tasks_async`).
  - `yanodes` (`entrypoints/cli/show_nodes.py`): the private `_NodeView.task_id`
    annotation narrows `int | None -> TaskId | None` (`show_nodes.py:56`); the
    join builder `_fetch_nodes_view` keeps `task_id=task.task_id if task else
    None` (`show_nodes.py:152`, now carries a `TaskId` rather than an int,
    mirroring how the `add-node-id-identity` change carries `NodeId` through
    `_NodeView`). The table renderer `"-" if row.task_id is None else
    str(row.task_id)` (`show_nodes.py:205`) is unchanged (`TaskId.__str__`
    renders the bare int). The JSON renderer's `{"task_id": r.task_id, ...}`
    (`show_nodes.py:241`) extracts `.value`: `{"task_id": r.task_id.value, ...}`
    so the public JSON stays `int`-typed.

- **No DB migration, no SQL query changes.** `yascheduler_tasks.task_id SERIAL
  PRIMARY KEY` and `task/insert.sql ... RETURNING task_id` already exist.

- **Out of scope (explicit non-goals):** changing the public `Yascheduler`
  facade signatures (frozen); switching `ConnectedMachine.ip` or any node-side
  identity (that is the `add-node-id-identity` change's territory); changing the
  `yascheduler_tasks` schema; revisiting the `_events` transient-field design;
  propagating `TaskId` into the AiiDA scheduler plugin entrypoint (it consumes
  the facade's `int`-typed API and is unaffected).

No **BREAKING** changes to public APIs. The `Yascheduler` facade / Python client
API is unchanged (signatures stay `int`; the int/TaskId conversion is internal
to the facade). The INI config format is unchanged. The DB schema is unchanged.
The internal `TaskRepository` Protocol, the use-case entry signatures, and the
domain events/exceptions narrow `int -> TaskId`; their consumers (orchestrator,
CLI, unit/integration/e2e tests) are updated in the same change. This is an
internal-Protocol narrowing, not a public-API change — symmetric to what
`add-node-id-identity` does for `NodeRepository`.

## Capabilities

### Modified Capabilities
- `domain-entities` — `Task.task_id: int -> task_id: TaskId`; add `NewTask`
  (pre-persistence) and `TaskId` (value object); importability scenario adds
  `NewTask, TaskId`.
- `domain-events` — `DomainEvent.task_id: int -> task_id: TaskId` (and the 5
  subclasses); event-construction scenarios use `TaskId(42)` literals.
- `domain-exceptions` — the 6 task-keyed domain exceptions take `TaskId` (was
  `int`); `e.task_id == TaskId(42)` scenarios.
- `postgres-repositories` — `PostgresTaskRepository`: `insert(NewTask) ->
  Task`, `get`/`update_status` take `TaskId`, `list_ids_by_ip_and_status ->
  list[TaskId]`, `list_by_jobs(list[TaskId])`, `_row_to_task` wraps `TaskId`,
  SQL params pass `.value`; the `insert(task_id=0)` scenario becomes
  `insert(NewTask)`.
- `use-cases` — `submit_task` return type `int -> TaskId`;
  `allocate_task(task_id: TaskId)`; `consume_task(task_id: TaskId)`.
- `package-facades` — the public `Yascheduler` facade stays `int`-typed on its
  public surface; it is declared the sole int/TaskId marshalling boundary
  (wraps `TaskId(...)` on input, extracts `.value` on output).
- `webhook-handler` — `webhook_handler`'s `WebhookPayload(task_id=event.task_id,
  ...)` construction at `webhook.py:86` extracts `.value` (`task_id=
  event.task_id.value`) so the `asdict`-serialized POST body keeps the
  `{"task_id": int, ...}` wire shape; `WebhookPayload.task_id: int` stays `int`.
  Event-construction scenarios update literals to `TaskId(42)` for consistency.
  The wire payload shape is preserved.

### Added Capabilities
- (none — `domain-entities` gains the `TaskId` and `NewTask` requirements
  within its existing scope; no new capability directories.)
